scope: Independent 24-shape exploratory screen of candidate entry against current default and GMP on a fixed platform and source snapshot; no production threshold follows from this screen alone or historical measurements

comparators.C: forced toom4_low::modular or toom4_square_low::low followed by normalize_top at every positive length; exploratory only
comparators.G: GMP mpn_mul_n or mpn_sqr, followed by low-half copy and identical top-bit mask

inputs: Identical deterministic operands per mode and run, seed 20261109 xor limbs xor top shifted 32; same immutable inputs, output length n and scratch capacities exactly 12n for product, 10n for square with surrounding canaries
allocation: Input, expected, output, and scratch buffers are allocated and populated before calibration and recorded batches; all modes reuse the same output and scratch slices; GMP writes its full result into scratch. No allocation is intentionally included in a timed call.
sampling: Two separate processes; seven repetitions for every operation and shape; G-ABBA-G then G-ACCA-G, or G-BAAB-G then G-CAAC-G, alternate within each run, starting ABBA/ACCA for run 0 and BAAB/CAAC for run 1; common iteration count calibrated to at least 20 ms and every retained batch at least 10 ms; no result-based retry or dropped samples
shapes: For both operations: top=63 at n=1,256,511,512,513,1023,1024,1025,1536,2047,2048,2049,3072,4095,4096,4097; top=1,31,64 at n=1024,2048; top=1,64 at n=4096. Exactly 24 distinct shapes, preregistered before timing.
identity: Full positive proof report, native snapshot, proof-exported library and metadata, measurement source, binary, rustc and its proof-recorded dynamic dependencies, fixed GCC/BFD linker tools and their dependencies, GMP and all other linked runtime libraries bound by SHA-256 before and after. The preparation report hashes every retained raw preparation log and code-generation artifact; verify those hashes before and after each run. Resolve runtime libraries in the fixed benchmark environment before each process; pause that live process at READY and DONE to compare the exact mapped path set, device/inode and hashes to the resolved set. Check its environment and mapping metadata every monitoring interval; reject system preload. Retain ldd output, maps, raw per-batch CSV and process monitoring. Between-sample transient mappings and Windows host activity remain outside this observation.
environment: Launch the Python timing controller through env -i with exactly PATH=/usr/bin:/bin LANG=C LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; the benchmark process and ldd use that same environment. All other inherited variables, including LD_*, GLIBC_TUNABLES and MALLOC_*, are absent. Build tools use the exact proof toolchain environment plus the fixed locale, time zone and single-thread settings, without inherited variables.
input_check: Before timing, run the same screen binary in no-timing mode on all 24 shapes and both operations, comparing all four modes against GMP on the exact deterministic timer inputs and checking canaries. The checks run again immediately before each shape's timed batches.
window: Parent schedules one quiet WSL window; single explicit CPU affinity and one benchmark thread; no other scheduled benchmark or heavy proof; preflight and continuous /proc process/aggregate monitoring, noting that WSL cannot observe all Windows host contention. An alarm limits the whole controller to 420 seconds, and each released benchmark process is limited to 180 seconds. Deadline or external termination kills the benchmark process group, waits for it, marks the complete window invalid, and preserves raw data; interrupted uninterruptible system calls do not provide hard realtime guarantees.

stop.busy: Sample while the benchmark is blocked before releasing it, and thereafter at each one-second interval. Abort if any other observed process or total non-benchmark guest busy time exceeds 10% of one CPU. Bound aggregate busy with /proc/stat readings before and after each process enumeration, so sampling order cannot underestimate guest CPU used by short-lived processes. No partial run is accepted
stop.invalid: Abort on failed result/canary comparison, batch under 10 ms, missing sample, timeout, process failure, source/tool/library drift, changed boot, CPU affinity failure or incomplete raw data
stop.drift: For every operation, shape, run and A/B/G or A/C/G block: each pair of A, B or C, and G batches has max/min <= 1.10. Separately for each order, the max/min of the repetition-level A, B or C, G, and (B or C)/A means is <= 1.10. Across the two orders, the max/min of each order's median A, B or C, and G is <= 1.10 and the max/min of the order-median (B or C)/A is <= 1.05. Between the two independent processes, max/min of run-median A, B or C, G <= 1.10 and of run-median (B or C)/A <= 1.05; the ratio medians for each order separately must also have between-run max/min <= 1.05. Any failure invalidates the entire window without selective retry.

candidate_policy: Report all B/A, C/A and GMP ratios and screening flags with no selective retry. The subset omits many registered and top-bit shapes; screening flags are exploratory only and do not establish that unsampled lengths benefit or that production regression gates pass. C/A is exploratory only and uses the paired A in its own block.
final_acceptance: A subsequent chosen production dispatch must be re-reviewed and reverified against its own final source, including default-path oracle, all top bits, alias, scratch/capacity, semantic mutations, code generation, boundary/regression and combination performance; backend GMP parity remains separate.
